blocks.text: The purpose of this document is to assist Cadence in understanding and operationalizing the enhancements made to its Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) capabilities through the implementation of the OneTrust TPRM solution. This engagement aims to provide Cadence with a standardized, scalable, and automated solution that aligns with its business, operational, and compliance requirements. l
As part of this engagement, Optiv supported the implementation and configuration of Cadence’s OneTrust TPRM instance. This comprises:
Designing and implementing structured workflows aligned with Cadence’s operational needs and TPRM requirements.
Configuring user roles to ensure appropriate access management.
Establishing vendor onboarding attributes to streamline supplier risk processes.
Refreshing and tailoring the Due Diligence Questionnaire to ensure alignment with Cadence’s risk assessment objectives and regulatory requirements.
Through this effort, Cadence will attain a more structured, transparent, and efficient TPRM framework, reducing manual effort and ensuring compliance with internal and external risk requirements.

The scope of this document focuses on Cadence’s TPRM processes, and the responsibilities of internal stakeholders involved in managing third-party risks. The following activities are included within this scope:

Current State Analysis: Review the current state of Cadence’s OneTrust TPRM instance, including its configuration, workflows, and supporting processes, while also assessing alignment with the broader TPRM program.
Refreshing the Due Diligence Questionnaire: Enhance and update existing questionnaires to align with Cadence’s organizational structure, compliance needs, and industry best practices.
Configuration of OneTrust TPRM: Document and configure custom workflows, rules, questionnaire templates, and notification processes in OneTrust tailored to Cadence’s requirements.

Training & Knowledge Transfer: Provide documentation covering OneTrust setup and configuration, workflow logics and questionnaire rules, ensuring Cadence stakeholders can effectively manage and operate the solution.

Building on the objectives outlined in Section 1, this section details the key enhancements implemented within Cadence’s OneTrust TPRM framework. These enhancements were designed to streamline vendor risk management, standardize due diligence processes, and improve visibility across the third-party lifecycle.

End-to-end workflows have been designed and implemented in OneTrust to manage the lifecycle of each third-party type. These workflows ensure that third parties are automatically directed through the appropriate due diligence questionnaires, approvals, and process based on their classification (e.g., third-party type).

Integration with Ironclad ensures that contract creation and execution trigger corresponding workflows in OneTrust, aligning contract and risk management activities.

The DDQ templates have been refreshed and aligned with Cadence’s requirements. The updated questionnaires capture critical information of the third party about data sensitivity, regulatory obligations, country risk, and geopolitical considerations.

A standardized risk tiering methodology has been embedded into OneTrust. This model integrates multiple factors (financial, operational, compliance, and security) and supports a consistent evaluation process for all third parties.

In addition to tiering, risk statements have been developed along with associated mitigation recommendations mapped to due diligence questions. These enable Cadence to not only identify potential risks but also track mitigation activities and ensure accountability through the OneTrust platform.

The implemented enhancements provide Cadence with a standardized, automated, and auditable TPRM framework within OneTrust. The key objectives achieved are:
Elimination of manual and fragmented processes.
Centralized vendor classification and workflow automation.
Refreshed due diligence questionnaires aligned with industry standards.
Consistent application of risk tiering and review cadences.
Enhanced visibility, compliance, and scalability of the TPRM program.

Through these enhancements, Cadence’s TPRM program has an efficient, and scalable framework that reduces risk exposure and ensures compliance with both internal policies and external regulatory requirements.

Currently, Cadence’s TPRM program is positioned at the “Siloed Risk Function” stage, where risk ownership and assessment activities are distributed across functions such as Legal, Compliance, Security, and Procurement. Each area maintains its own risk processes, resulting in fragmented oversight.

The strategic objective of this engagement is to transition Cadence toward the “Integrated Risk Management (IRM)” stage - where all third-party risks are collectively managed through a unified, automated, and standardized framework within OneTrust. This will establish a single source of truth for vendor risk visibility, governance, and decision-making.
A key enabler of this transformation is the integration between Ironclad and OneTrust, which connects contract lifecycle management with third-party risk workflows. Through this integration:
Contract creation and execution in Ironclad automatically triggers corresponding due diligence and assessment workflows in OneTrust.
Vendor-related data (e.g., contract terms, renewal dates, risk tier, and compliance status) synchronizes between systems for continuous visibility.
Risk and contractual obligations are managed cohesively within a single ecosystem.
Optiv’s implementation approach supports this evolution by consolidating all risk-related processes into OneTrust and aligning them with two primary risk domains:

Identified through due diligence questionnaires covering Legal, Financial, Privacy, and Compliance areas. These assessments capture vendor-level dependencies, regulatory exposures, and process inefficiencies at both organizational and product/service levels.
Identified through security questionnaires focusing on data protection, access control, incident management, and infrastructure security.
By structuring risk assessments around these two domains, and integrating Ironclad with OneTrust, Cadence can now:
Manage operational and cybersecurity risks in a unified workstream.
Automate due diligence, escalation, and remediation workflows.
Maintain cross-functional visibility across all risk stakeholders.
Strengthen accountability through consistent, platform-driven governance.
Progress toward a mature Integrated Risk Management model that aligns risk oversight with Cadence’s business objectives and growth strategy.

Cadence’s third-party workflows in OneTrust are now fully automated and tailored to the criticality and type of vendor.

Third parties are classified based on data sensitivity and risk criticality, with separate workflows established for Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 vendors. Tier 3 third parties typically represent lower-risk engagements (e.g., limited data access or short-term service contracts), while Tiers 1 and 2 represent medium- and high-risk third parties requiring enhanced due diligence.

Additionally, classification by third-party Category ensures that distinct workflows are automatically triggered for Staffing Vendors, Service Providers, Marketing Partners, Revenue Partners, and International Vendors.

When a new third-party is added to the OneTrust platform, it is routed through an automated onboarding workflow that analyzes both third-party tier and category. Based on these attributes, the system assigns the appropriate workflow path for due diligence, assessment, and approval.

Cadence’s OneTrust environment has been configured with automated workflows that manage the lifecycle of third-party assessments based on both vendor category and risk tier. The integration between Ironclad and OneTrust ensures that every new vendor entering the system is automatically analyzed and assigned to the appropriate workflow.

Vendors tiered under Tier 1 and Tier 2 undergo a comprehensive due diligence process, differentiated by data criticality and risk profile. The following vendor categories fall under this group: Staffing Vendors, Service Providers and Vendors, Marketing Partners, Revenue Partners, and International Vendors. Each category is assigned a tailored due diligence questionnaire, which is automatically sent to the Primary Vendor Contact upon workflow initiation.

Tier 3 third parties are subject to a simplified due diligence process, reflecting their lower criticality and risk exposure. A distinct questionnaire is designed for this tier, focusing on essential operational and security controls.

Note: Renewal and offboarding processes are incorporated into the above workflows based on the tier of the third party. The offboarding workflow currently sends notifications to relevant stakeholders for review and approval of offboarding actions.

For future iterations, Cadence may consider expanding automation by developing an integration with Torii to streamline the offboarding workflow through API-triggered deprovisioning and asset revocation.

Questionnaire development is a one-time configuration activity performed in OneTrust. Once developed, the questionnaires can be reused across multiple assessments. These questionnaires can be workflow specific or third-party specific, depending on the organization’s requirements.

As per Cadence’s requirements, two questionnaires were developed each aligned with the third-party tiering model to support automated due diligence activities. These questionnaires are designed to gather detailed information from vendors based on their assigned tier and risk exposure. Both questionnaires are accessible within the Templates section of the Third-Party Risk Management module in OneTrust.
Due Diligence Questionnaire T1–2 v1 – Applicable for Tier 1 and Tier 2 third parties.
Due Diligence Questionnaire T3 v1 – Applicable for Tier 3 third parties.

This document also includes details of the rules applied within the questionnaire template. These rules should be referenced and updated as required for any future implementations or modifications to the template. The rules control question behavior, such as conditional visibility and response-based logic, ensuring that subsequent questions appear only when relevant answers are selected.

Navigate to the “Templates” section within the “Third-Party Risk Management” module.

Within the Due Diligence Questionnaire T1–2 v1 template, a total of eight sections were developed, each containing approved questions mapped to Cadence’s TPRM requirements. These sections cover diverse operational and risk areas to ensure a comprehensive evaluation of third parties.
Scenario 1: Launching (Showing) follow-up questions depending on selection of “Yes”.
Conditional logic, also known as “Show logic,” has been configured across the questionnaire to trigger follow-up questions based on the respondent’s selections.

When a question requires a Yes/No response, selecting “Yes” automatically launches additional follow-up questions for detailed input, while selecting “No” hides those dependent questions. This ensures that the questionnaire remains dynamic and relevant to the vendor’s response profile.
To add conditional logic for such scenarios, the following steps can be executed:
Select “Show logic” in the “Details” tab and click “Save.”
Click on the “Show logic” symbol for the question where logic is to be applied.

In the above scenario, if “Yes” is selected for question 4.4 (Condition), then question 4.5 will be automatically displayed to the user (Action). The configuration details of these conditions and actions are documented in Appendix C.
Scenario 2: Launching multiple questions after answering one question

If multiple questions are to be displayed based on the response to a single question, the “Copy logic to additional questions” option can be utilized. This enables the logic applied to one question to be extended to other related questions, streamlining configuration efforts.

For example, as per Cadence’s requirements, this logic is applied to questions related to Artificial Intelligence (AI). When the initial AI-related question is answered, three additional follow-up questions are automatically launched to gather more specific details.
This configuration allows efficient reuse of logic rules and helps maintain questionnaire consistency across related risk domains.

The method of adding rules is applied individually to all logic-based questions and documented in Appendix C. The configuration team has maintained distinct logic rules for each scenario to simplify future maintenance. This approach allows easier modification or removal of rules while minimizing the risk of errors during updates or version changes.

Adding Risk controls: Determining the correct risk scoring and associated controls is critical, as it influences the mitigation timeline and monitoring cadence. To add a control for a documented risk, follow the steps below:

Click “Save” once the control information is finalized.

The control becomes linked to the risk within OneTrust and is displayed whenever the risk is triggered during an assessment. This ensures consistent tracking and documentation of mitigation measures across third parties and assessments.

The workflows have been developed based on the attributes “Vendor Tier” and “Vendor Category.” This section outlines the configuration process for creating and managing workflows within OneTrust, as determined by the details mentioned in Section 4.2.

Each workflow governs the automation of specific vendor management activities such as onboarding, assessment, renewal, and offboarding. These workflows ensure that third parties are appropriately categorized and routed through the correct due diligence process.
To create a new workflow in OneTrust, follow the steps below:
Click on the “Workflow” section in the left navigation panel.
Click on the “View” button under the “Vendor Workflows” tile.
Click on “Default Onboarding Workflow” (a new workflow can also be created directly).
Click on the “Clone” button located in the top-right corner of the screen.

Cloning an existing workflow (or creating a new one) will generate a draft version within the Vendor Workflow page. This draft can then be customized further to match the expected workflow design and requirements.
Once the new workflow is created, it will appear under the Vendor Workflows menu. To configure it, open the workflow and modify its stages as required.
Follow the steps below to update the stages for the onboarding workflow:
Delete any unnecessary stages using the delete icon on the stage name tile.
Rename “Stage 1” to “New Third Party” using the edit option in the Stage Details tab.
Retain the Live stage as the final stage.
This configuration ensures that the onboarding workflow includes the necessary entry and exit points to handle vendor initiation and post-assessment activation within OneTrust.

The above setup represents the basic structure of the onboarding workflow. The same approach can be followed to configure or edit stages for other workflows, such as Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 workflows.
Once stages are defined, additional automation rules and triggers are added within the workflow tabs. These rules control actions such as:
Advancing workflow stages automatically based on responses.
Changing workflow paths (for reassessments or renewals).
This stage-wise automation ensures smooth progression of vendors through their respective assessment processes.

Before adding rules to the onboarding workflow, all other workflows (for Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 third parties) must be developed and finalized. This is because the onboarding workflow relies on these workflows for routing vendors to the correct due diligence stream.
Therefore, it is essential to first complete and publish the Tier-specific workflows before assigning them to the onboarding workflow configuration.
Once all workflows are created and validated, they can be viewed in the Vendor Workflows list.

Note: A workflow should only be published after all rules, triggers, and automation logic have been configured and validated. Publishing prematurely may lead to incomplete routing or broken dependencies within the automation.

When a new assessment is sent to the Primary Vendor Contact, it must be completed within the specified timeline.
User Groups are responsible for reviewing the responses provided by the Primary Vendor Contact in the questionnaire and for analyzing any flagged risks.

The Primary Vendor Contact must provide a response within the defined timeframe to address a documented high risk. This stage is for acknowledging and analyzing the risk, it is not a remediation period. (The calculation for this duration starts after deadline period for Review Responses (4 days, see SLA.2). Therefore, actual deadline will be 5+4 = 9 days)

The Primary Vendor Contact must provide a response within the defined timeframe to address a documented medium risk. This stage is for acknowledging and analyzing the risk, it is not a remediation period. (The calculation for this duration starts after deadline period for Review Responses (4 days, see SLA.2). Therefore, actual deadline will be 10+4 = 14 days)

The Primary Vendor Contact must provide a response within the defined timeframe to address a documented low risk. This stage is for acknowledging and analyzing the risk, it is not a remediation period. (The calculation for this duration starts after deadline period for Review Responses (4 days, see SLA.2). Therefore, actual deadline will be 15+4 = 19 days)
